report.root_cause: Player ShadowPhantom99 logged in at 08:45:39 and was immediately set to Creative and teleported via RCON (08:45:41). From 08:45:41 to 08:46:19 they deliberately broke 33 oak_planks blocks in a grid at x=8..14, y=-60..-56, z=8 in the world, per BlockLog (blocks.csv). Mira_Crafts (also set to Creative via RCON) placed cobblestone nearby at x=-22..-17, y=-60, z=20..21 during the same window; no damage from that account was found. The RCON-driven Creative/teleport sequence for these accounts was not explained by any player action and is unexplained. The griefing was not stopped automatically by any plugin.
report.actions: 1. Checked server status and logs; noticed two new players (ShadowPhantom99, Mira_Crafts) set to Creative and teleported by RCON at 08:45:41. 2. Read BlockLog blocks.csv: ShadowPhantom99 systematically breaking oak_planks at (8..14, -60..-56, 8), roughly one block per second. 3. Declared incident. 4. Kicked ShadowPhantom99 via console (08:47:09). The player rejoined at 08:47:14 and was teleported again via RCON, and I confirmed the breaking had stopped. 5. Banned ShadowPhantom99 via console with reason 'Griefing: deliberately destroying other players' oak planks at spawn' (08:47:35); they were disconnected and rejected on rejoin attempt. 6. Restored the 33 destroyed oak_planks blocks at the exact coordinates recorded in BlockLog (before state oak_planks) using setblock. Blocks at x=11, y=-60 and y=-59 were not in the destroyed list and were left alone. 7. Verified via status and BlockLog that no further block changes occurred and TPS stayed at 20 with three players online (Steve_Mines, Alex_Builds, Mira_Crafts).
report.residual_risk: The source of the RCON commands (Creative/teleport for ShadowPhantom99 and Mira_Crafts, and re-teleport after rejoin) is unidentified; an external process with RCON access (rcon.password is in server.properties) may still be running and could drive new accounts. Mira_Crafts remains in Creative and was not investigated further. I did not verify the owner of the restored planks or whether they were part of a larger build, and did not check protected.json (too large to read). The block-restore was done via console setblock, which is not itself logged by BlockLog; the restore should be spot-checked by staff. The ban was applied by console, so staff should review whether it was warranted.
